notes: Read SKILL.md in full (the only file). Git workflow guidance: trunk-based development, atomic commits with conventional messages, branch naming, worktrees for parallel agents, save-point pattern, change summaries, pre-commit hygiene, git debugging, and semantic versioning/tagging/changelogs.

Medium because following it makes the agent perform state-changing git operations: commits, branch/worktree creation and removal (SKILL.md:153-164), reverting to the last commit with `git reset --hard HEAD` when a test fails (SKILL.md:180-189), and pushing release tags to the remote (SKILL.md:291-292). Acceptable because these are standard, user-requested version-control actions on the user's own repository; the reset is framed as discarding only the agent's latest uncommitted increment under a commit-every-slice discipline, the push targets the user's own origin, and force-pushing to shared branches is listed as a red flag. Users with their own uncommitted work in the tree should be aware the save-point revert discards uncommitted changes.

Pre-commit hygiene runs the project's npm test/lint/tsc and greps the staged diff for secret-looking strings (SKILL.md:215-229); no installs, credentials or downloads. Optional pointers to sibling skills (code-review-and-quality, api-and-interface-design, deprecation-and-migration, shipping-and-launch); the ../ paths at SKILL.md:153-164 are example worktree locations, not links to required files.

Lead reviewer: SKILL.md:189 mentions git reset --hard HEAD as the way back to the last good state; it discards uncommitted work, so the agent should confirm with the user first. Released as medium with this note.
